Adolescent depressive and anxiety symptoms, ages 12–16 (simulated)

depression.Rd

Depressive and anxiety symptoms of 600 adolescents at five annual waves with covariates and two outcomes at age 21, designed for latent class growth analysis and growth mixture models (growth()), including quadratic trajectories and parallel processes, with covariates and distal outcomes.

Usage

depression

Format

A data frame with 600 rows and 16 columns:

id

Adolescent id.

dep1, dep2, dep3, dep4, dep5

Depressive symptoms (CES-D-10, 0–30) at ages 12, 13, 14, 15, 16.

anx1, anx2, anx3, anx4, anx5

Anxiety symptoms (GAD-7, 0–21) at the same ages.

female

1 = girl.

low_ses

Low family socioeconomic status (0/1).

aces

Number of adverse childhood experiences, 0–8.

distress21

Psychological distress at age 21 (K10, 10–50); 12 percent missing.

mde21

Major depressive episode by age 21 (0/1); 12 percent missing.

Attrition is monotone and more likely after high symptoms (missing at random); observed cases per wave 600, 574, 544, 509, 491.

Source

Simulated by datasets/generate.jl of LatentMixtures.jl (seed Xoshiro(20261104)); codebook in its datasets/README.md. Four trajectory classes (time = age - 12) with depression means (intercept, linear, quadratic): Low stable (sample share 0.537; 4.0, 0.3, 0), Increasing (0.273; 5.0, 2.6, -0.25), Decreasing (0.097; 14.0, -2.0, 0.10), Chronic high (0.093; 15.0, 0.6, 0); anxiety means (3.0, 0.2, 0), (4.0, 1.5, -0.10), (10.0, -1.2, 0), (11.0, 0.3, 0). Random intercepts, slopes and a small random quadratic term, correlated across the two processes and equal across classes; residual standard deviations 2.5 and 2.0. Girls and adolescents with more ACEs are more likely to be in the Increasing and Chronic classes. Outcomes depend on the class only: mean distress21 15, 20, 17, 25; P(mde21) .08, .25, .12, .40. Modelled on Brendgen et al. (2005, J. Abnormal Child Psychology 33, 579–594, doi:10.1007/s10802-005-6739-2 ) and Shore et al. (2018, Child and Adolescent Mental Health 23(2), 107–120, doi:10.1111/camh.12220 ). Licence: CC0 1.0 (public domain).

Examples

data(depression)
# mean depressive symptoms rise from age 12 to 16
colMeans(depression[, paste0("dep", 1:5)], na.rm = TRUE)
#>     dep1     dep2     dep3     dep4     dep5 
#> 6.480000 6.972125 7.591912 7.972495 8.346232 
# \donttest{
# which depressive-symptom trajectories are there? linear LCGA, 4 classes
g <- growth(depression, dep1:dep5, K = 4)
#> Starting Julia ...
growthparams(g)$alpha  # intercept (age 12) and annual slope of each class
#>              class1   class2    class3    class4
#> intercept 3.7024811 5.756453 13.565031 14.883145
#> linear    0.2854458 1.583889 -1.392196  0.706383
# }
